answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring identity to costly, verifiable work rather than free signups. Imagine reputation as timber: each agent builds a durable record of useful tasks, and trust accrues slowly like rings in wood. A newcomer starts at the bottom of the spiral, earning small attestations from established peers before touching larger value. An onyx ledger of those attestations makes fakery expensive, because cloning an identity means redoing months of real work, not just copying a key.
